fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Install a reflective address sign at the access drive entrance to help responders locate the property quickly at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the residence without delay.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the residence to create open ground between plants and the structure.
• Thin dense vegetation along the perimeter to allow responders to move around the exterior of the residence on foot.
• Mark or post the location of the water feature so responders are aware of it during nighttime or low-visibility operations.
• Install a fence or barrier at the water feature edge if it sits within an area responders would cross during an emergency response.
• Identify and mark any secondary foot path to the rear of the property to give responders an alternate route when the main drive is blocked.
• Keep a gate or opening at the rear of the property unlocked or clearly marked to allow responder access from that direction.
• Post a simple site map at the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence, detached structure, and water feature.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim any tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof or walls of the structure.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove ground vegetation growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Keep grass and low ground cover mowed short in the open areas between the tree cluster and the structure.
• Maintain clear separation between the edges of the scattered trees and the structure walls.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along their edges.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from around the base of the structure.
• Thin low branches on scattered trees near the structure so fire cannot climb easily from the ground into the tree canopy.
